Analysis by Richard Cowan 

From the beginning, MarijuanaNews.com has carried regular reports on the success of the Dutch experience. 

See 

Dutch Developments: Police Union Protests Cannabis Policies. Farmers Diversify. Mayors and Police Chiefs Call for UN Policy Review. Only In Holland. 

and links. 

And there have also been regular reports on the Drug War disaster in Mexico. See 

Hitmen Wanted. Violence Of Prohibition Helps Recruit Zetas As U.S. State Department Warns About “Military Small-Unit Combat” On Mexican Border. 

Recently, I have contrasted the situations in the two countries. 

See 

Tale of Two Countries, The Netherlands and Mexico, Regulation Versus Violence. Dutch Cannabis Smokers To Go “American”? When Will the Murders Cross Our Border? 

Fortunately, there is more good news from the Dutch. 

Yesterday, the Dutchnews.nl reported that the outgoing chairman of the Dutch police union (NPB) Hans van Duijn called for the legalization of cannabis, meaning licensed growing to supply the licensed retail system, because the present practice of trying to outlaw growing “only leads to more crime.” (He also in favor of “letting long time addicts use hard drugs under supervision.”) 

He says that this is the only way to effectively fight drug related crime, which takes “a great deal of the police's time and energy and other crime issues suffer from it.”

 

He said that most senior police officers feel the same way, but Dutch politicians are reluctant to consider legalizing cannabis, because of “international pressure they prefer to put their heads in the sand.” That is entirely consistent with what I have heard over the last several years. 

Unfortunately, there is also more bad news from Mexico, just when you thought it couldn’t get any worse. 

The McClatchy Newspapers are carrying a well-written story by Franco Ordonez, Kidnappings soar in Mexico as drug gangs seek new income. 

The situation in Juarez, just across from El Paso, is truly frightening.

See

Drug War Carnage In Mexico Grows As Dozens of Bodies Found In Buried Mass Graves Just South of El Paso. At Least 3,000 Thousand More Killed Since 2006. 

According to Ordonez, “Corporate security experts estimate that drug gangs are now responsible for 30 to 50 kidnappings a day in Mexico and that ransoms often run to $300,000 if the victim is returned alive. They often hold several victims at a time… 

The phenomenon is spilling over into the United States . Phoenix police investigated more than 350 kidnappings last year, a 40 percent increase from the year before.”. 

Incredibly, Mexican officials see these kidnappings as a sign of success in the Drug War! 

"Drug trafficking is not producing for them as it did in the past," Mexican Attorney General Eduardo Medina Mora said last month in Washington . "So they are moving into other crimes, such as extortion, kidnapping, car theft." 

See 

Walters Agrees to Help Major Mexican Organized Crime By Prosecuting More Small Marijuana Smugglers. Lock My People Up, Says Mexican AG. The Drug War Really Is About Marijuana. 

However, Ordonez observes that “the rise in kidnappings also shows that Mexico's law enforcement problems go beyond narcotics. Distrust of the police, who may be involved in some of the abductions, and fear that victims will be harmed make kidnapping one of Mexico's most underreported crimes. 

Mexican officials say that only a third of kidnappings are reported to police, but corporate experts say it's more like one in 10... The failure to report is related to the perception of inefficiency, corruption and injustice that exists in the penal justice system. 

That means that drug gangs can kidnap almost with impunity.” 

The damage done by the Drug War in both the US and Mexico will take many years to repair – after the war finally stops. 

Meanwhile, in another border city, it is only the sick and dying who have to live in fear… of the San Diego police, who simply will not obey state laws. 

See 

Hugely Important California Supreme Court Ruling Ignored by Media. State Officials Must Obey State – Not Federal – Law. 

The violent crime rate in San Diego is actually a bit below the national average, but there are still more than 20 violent crimes – robberies, assaults, rapes and murders – per day in the city. Despite these real crimes, the San Diego police are now trapping medical cannabis delivery services, after having shut down the dispensaries. 

The police call and falsely identify themselves as patients and then confiscate both cash and cannabis from the drivers, and threaten that "one more delivery and we're inviting the feds in to look at this." None of the drivers have been arrested, and I doubt if the Feds would be interested, but where did the cash and cannabis go? Would it be worse if the police were stealing or “just following orders”? 

See 

Annotated NORML Weekly News for March 13, 2008. Swedes Find Zero Tolerance = Zero Value. Rhode Island Legislature Considers Compassion Centers. San Diego Rejects Compassion. 

As they used to say… Compare and contrast the situation in the three countries.
